title: Compatibilities of Weil equivariance
statement:
All geometric- and scheme-Frobenius equivariance squares of
[thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] and of
[prop-pur-weil-equivariance-scheme-frobenius] commute with finite
reduction, scalar extension, composition, and base change.

proof.text: Keep exactly the domains of the named geometric squares: separated finite-type geometric schemes, smooth $f$ of pure dimension $d$, and strict constructible finite-Tor data at the specified completed/localized coefficient stages. Apply [lem-pur-weil-coefficient-diagram-identifications]. Its two recovery identities specify the exceptional datum and counit from purity and trace, while its source, semilinear-exchange and coefficient equations identify every arrow of the geometric squares under finite reduction and scalar extension. Thus both coefficient compatibilities concern the prescribed diagrams, including integral-to-finite reduction and common finite field stages.

For composable smooth maps of dimensions $d,e$, apply [lem-pur-weil-composite-diagram-identifications]. Its source identification retains the $e$-twist during the $f$-trace. Its purity and trace composition identities and the compact-support datum identification compare the pasted squares. The displayed counit equation, under the specified exceptional composition $c$ and compact-support composition $\alpha$, identifies the pasted counit as well. The exceptional data and counits it reconstructs from purity and trace are the actual ones of the three squares by the recovery identities of [lem-pur-weil-coefficient-diagram-identifications] (Step 1). Hence all three geometric squares have the required composition compatibility.

For a Cartesian base change with compatible finite-field data apply [lem-pur-weil-basechange-diagram-identifications] on the named comparison domains. Its conjugation equation identifies the exceptional datum under $B_E$; its four-line counit identity identifies the counit under $B_E,B_F$. Its source, purity, trace and mixed semilinear-exchange equations identify the other arrows. As in Step 2, the reconstructed exceptional data and counits are the actual ones by the recovery identities of [lem-pur-weil-coefficient-diagram-identifications]. Consequently the base-changed geometric diagrams are exactly the prescribed diagrams for $f'$; no comparison domain is enlarged.

Apply [lem-pur-weil-kappa-coefficient-coherence] to every arrow and comparison just identified. Its coefficient/pullback equations and strict-tower realization permit precomposition by the specified $\kappa$, and its equivariant-arrow identity preserves composition and pasting. By [prop-pur-weil-equivariance-scheme-frobenius] these precomposed diagrams are precisely the three scheme-Frobenius diagrams. They therefore have the same four compatibilities. This uses the natural comparison of pullbacks, without applying Cartesian exchange to a scheme-Frobenius square.
